items.title: Each ask runs through the existing afkv2 lanes

props.text: When does the afkv2 agent send a milestone to the main agent?
**A.** The afkv2 agent decides: a committed change whose own tests pass and which can be used for 1 named purpose.
**B.** Only when the developer says so in the afkv2 pane.
**C.** The afkv2 agent proposes it in the afkv2 pane; it goes out on the developer's yes.
It never waits on the developer, and the developer still decides in the main pane whether to try it.
props.label: Recommended: A

settled.reading: Option a: the afkv2 agent decides a milestone. The main agent applies it at its earliest convenience on its own, and only tells the developer that it applied it and how to try it; it asks nothing.

props.text: herdr types a prompt into a working agent; it refuses only an agent that shows a dialog (herdr 0.9.5 `agent prompt --help`). Whether Claude or Codex then queues the text or changes the current turn is not verified.
**A.** Send at once with `herdr agent prompt`, even while the main agent works.
**B.** The afkv2 agent waits, in a background job, until the main pane is idle, then sends the note. Same path for Claude and Codex.
**C.** Write the note to a file only; the main agent reads it at the start of its next turn.
It never cuts into the main turn, and its wake is the exit of a background job, which both harnesses deliver; c has no wake.
props.label: Recommended: B

items.title: How the note reaches a busy main agent

props.text:
The note names each changed file by its worktree path and says how to use it. The main agent then:

- a changed or new skill: reads the `SKILL.md` from the worktree path and follows it in place of the installed copy, for the rest of the session; its scripts run from there too, because each script finds the plugin root from its own path (`afkv2/skills/small-change/scripts/small_lane.py:22`).
- a change to the core behaviors: reads the changed text and follows it as a session instruction.
- a change to a hook or `hooks.json`: cannot apply ad hoc, because hooks run from the installed plugin (`afkv2/hooks/hooks.json:11`). The note says so; the developer tries it after a release.

The applied changes end with the main session.

settled.reading: Accepted. A hook change applies best effort only. When a hook change is critical, the developer and the agents work out a reinstall of the plugin for that session, case by case; the skill does not automate it. afkv2 changes favour instructions over scripts, so most changes apply ad hoc.

props.text: You said you talk to the afkv2 agent yourself. But the trial and its evidence (errors, logs, output) sit in the main pane.
**A.** Only in the afkv2 pane.
**B.** In either pane. Feedback given in the main pane goes to the afkv2 agent with the evidence the main agent saw, by the same idle-wait path.
**C.** Only in the main pane; the main agent forwards everything.
The main agent holds the evidence of the trial; a copy by hand costs the developer work.
props.label: Recommended: B

props.text: Where the afkv2 work lands
**A.** 1 branch, worktree and Draft change into the plugin's integration branch per ask.
**B.** 1 branch for the whole pane session, all asks on it.
The owner rule: no unrelated changes on one branch (decision of 2026-10-27); each ask then merges or drops alone.
props.label: Recommended: A

**A.** Setup writes a new install record line `source <path>`.
**B.** The skill asks the developer each time.
**C.** The skill asks once, and writes the answer to the install record.
No setup change for machines that never dogfood, and 1 question per machine.
props.label: Recommended: C

items.title: What implementor tier means for the afkv2 agent

props.text: The developer tells the main agent that the main work is done. The main agent asks the afkv2 agent to wrap up: commit, push each Draft change, and report the open asks. Then the main agent closes the pane. Worktrees and branches stay for the developer, and `/afkv2:gc` cleans them after a merge. The pane lives past each result, which is an exception to playbook rule H-8; the skill states it.
The skill needs a pane the developer can see and talk to. Outside herdr (`HERDR_ENV` not 1, or no `herdr` on the path), it refuses with the reason and starts nothing (playbook H-9).

- **afkv2 agent**: the agent in the side pane that builds an afkv2 change while the developer works elsewhere.
- **Main agent**: the developer's session of the real work that opened the afkv2 agent. (Branch 204 uses the same word more widely; this ticket uses only this meaning.)
- **Milestone**: a committed afkv2 change that can be used for 1 named purpose, not released.
- **Milestone note**: the message from the afkv2 agent to the main agent: what changed, the worktree paths, how to use it, and what cannot apply ad hoc.
- **Apply ad hoc**: the main agent uses the changed files from the worktree in place of the installed copy, for the rest of its session.

You chose 1 branch for the pane session. The existing lanes each assume their own branch: the medium lane puts its spec folder on a feature branch and its plan on a separate run branch (`<feature branch>-run`), and the small lane starts its lane record per worktree. Counter-argument to your pick: with 1 branch, 1 Draft change holds every ask, so 1 ask cannot merge while another is half done, and 1 review covers unrelated work.
**A.** 1 branch and 1 Draft change per pane session; each ask is a small lane on it, with no grill and no plan; an ask that grows past small stops and is proposed as its own ticket.
**B.** 1 branch per pane session for small asks; an ask that needs the medium lane gets its own branch.
**C.** Back to 1 branch per ask.
Your pick holds for the common case, and a feature-sized ask keeps the lane it needs.

- **Developer**: starts the skill, talks to both agents, ends the pane.
- **Main agent**: opens and closes the afkv2 pane, forwards feedback, applies each milestone by reading files from the worktree. **Denied:** writing any plugin file; it changes nothing in the worktree.
- **afkv2 agent**: writes only in its plugin worktree, commits and pushes the Draft change. **Denied:** writing in the work repository, prompting any pane but the main agent's, merging.
- **Validation**: a milestone note must name at least 1 worktree path and 1 way to use it; a note for a hook change says best effort.

**Stories**
1. The developer asks the main agent for an afkv2 change, and keeps working while the afkv2 agent builds it.
2. The afkv2 agent sends a milestone, and the main agent applies it and tells the developer how to try it.
3. The developer gives feedback in either pane, and the afkv2 agent refines the change.
4. A new ask comes while the pane runs.
5. The main work ends, and the pane wraps up.

**Frequent:** in core-services the developer asks for a clearer step in `/afkv2:small-change`. The afkv2 agent edits its `SKILL.md`, commits, and sends: "changed: <worktree>/afkv2/skills/small-change/SKILL.md step 4; use it at your next small change". After its current step, the main agent says: "applied the small-change update; next small change uses it".

**Edge:** a second ask arrives while the first is half built. The afkv2 agent queues it, tells the developer in its pane, and starts it when the first reaches a milestone.

**Risky:** a milestone changes a skill that the main agent is running right now, mid-step. The main agent finishes the current step on the old text, then switches to the new text from the next step on, and says so. A milestone that changes a hook: the note says best effort, and the main agent tells the developer it may not apply in this session.
